title: Efficient Frequency Domain-based Transformers for High-Quality Image Deblurring
layout_note: Inverted U: in panel (a) the encoder is a tower of stacked slabs rising on the left and the decoder a tower descending on the right, joined by one solid arrow across the top; panels (b) and (c) and a legend box sit to the right in a single row, divided by vertical dashed lines.
grouping: Panel (a) splits the two towers onto two large rounded background panels, light grey for the left tower and light blue for the right. Panels (a), (b), (c) and the legend are separated by vertical dashed rules and labelled (a)/(b)/(c) underneath. Each detail panel sits on a rounded background tinted in its module's legend colour (pink for (b), light orange for (c)); inside (c) the FFT and W boxes are wrapped in a smaller purple rounded inset. Box fills follow colour families keyed by the legend (grey convolution, orange DFFN, pink FSAS, blue downsample, green upsample).
shapes_depth: Panel (a) draws every stage as a thin 3-D slab (a tilted parallelogram plane with visible edge thickness), stacked in coloured layers per level, with the input and output photos drawn as tilted planes in the same perspective. Panels (b) and (c) are flat: small rounded rectangles with thin dark outlines and pastel fills, Conv1x1 drawn as a green trapezoid, operators as circle glyphs, and the residual path as a right-angled line along the panel edge. Skip connections are dash-dot lines; main-path arrows are solid. No drop shadows.
proposed_highlight: The proposed modules are named in bold labels beside their slabs in (a) ("DFFN", "FSAS+DFFN") and carry their own colours (pink FSAS, orange DFFN); each is expanded in its own detail panel whose whole background is that colour, and both colours appear as entries in the boxed legend.
lesson: Each module's expanded detail panel is filled with that module's own legend colour (pink FSAS panel, orange DFFN panel), so the overview slab, the legend swatch and the zoomed panel read as one thing without any connector lines.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: Panel (a) puts the encoder as a rising tower of tilted slabs on a grey rounded panel and the decoder as a descending tower on a blue panel, with panels (b) FSAS and (c) DFFN and a legend box set off to the right by vertical dashed rules.
insights.data: The blurry input photo and the deblurred output are drawn as tilted image slabs at the foot of each tower, matching the 3-D slab style of the feature maps above them, with channel=48/96/192 written beside each level.
insights.emphasis: Each detail panel is tinted in its module's legend colour (pink FSAS, orange DFFN) and the FFT/W step in (c) is wrapped in a purple inset, so the frequency-domain parts pop out of otherwise pastel boxes.
insights.flow: In (a) data climbs the left tower, crosses at the top by one long arrow and descends the right tower, with dash-dot skip lines running horizontally into circled-C concatenations; (b) and (c) read top-to-bottom with a residual line looping around the right edge.
insights.avoid: The legend explains colour by op type but the slabs' stacked colour layers (pink/orange/green) are hard to map to block order, and the dash-dot skips are thin and easy to lose against the panel tints.

arrangement.units: three lettered panels separated by vertical dashed rules: (a) the network on two rounded tinted backgrounds (grey encoder, blue decoder), (b) FSAS on a pink rounded panel, (c) DFFN on an orange rounded panel
arrangement.inputs_as: tilted real blurry photo slab at the bottom of the encoder tower
arrangement.shared: colour legend shared by all panels
